videos.caption: You do NOT need to build a complicated website before selling your first digital product. There are plenty of beginner-friendly platforms that can handle the selling and delivery for you. Here are 7 places to consider: 1. Stan Store Great for creators selling ebooks, guides, templates, courses, and other digital products through social media. 2. Etsy Useful if you want your products to be discoverable through marketplace search. Think planners, printables, invitations, templates, and worksheets. 3. Gumroad Simple option for selling ebooks, guides, templates, files, memberships, and other downloads. 4. Beacons Lets you create a link-in-bio storefront and sell digital products directly from it. 5. Shopify Better if you want more control over your store, branding, and customer experience as your business grows. 6. Payhip Beginner-friendly platform for selling downloads, courses, memberships, and other digital products. 7. Systeme.io Useful if you want your products, sales funnels, email marketing, and automations in one place. The platform matters, but don’t let choosing one keep you stuck. Pick ONE. Upload ONE useful product. Start creating content that attracts the people who need it. You can always upgrade your setup later. SAVE this for when you’re ready to sell your first digital product. #digitalproducts #selldigitalproducts #facelessmarketing #digitalproductbusiness #facelessbusiness

If I had to make my first $5K this month with digital products, I would NOT start by creating everything from scratch. Here’s the exact PLR path I’d follow: 1️⃣ Choose ONE audience. 2️⃣ Find ONE urgent problem they’re already searching for help with. 3️⃣ Purchase a quality PLR product that solves that problem. 4️⃣ Rebrand it with a new title, cover, examples, and my own voice. 5️⃣ Add a bonus that makes the offer feel like a no-brainer. 6️⃣ Price it at $57. Your digital product checkout is more than a payment button. 👀 If you sell ebooks, templates, courses, guides, Canva templates, or other digital products, you need to think about what happens after someone clicks “buy.” Before selling your first digital product, make sure you have: 1️⃣ Purchase terms — what the customer is actually agreeing to when they buy. 2️⃣ License & use restrictions — what they can and cannot do with your product. 3️⃣ Privacy Policy — especially if you’re collecting customer information. 4️⃣ Website/store terms — the rules governing purchases and use of your store. 5️⃣ Protection against unauthorized sharing & reselling — because your digital product should not become the internet’s free download. 😭 Your creativity is an asset. Treat it like one. And remember: your legal protection shouldn’t start after someone steals or misuses your digital product. It should be part of your business from the beginning.
